 By Juan Ortega | South Florida Sun Sentinel and Angie DiMichele | adimichele@sunsentinel.com | South Florida Sun Sentinel PUBLISHED: November 17, 2026 at 8:26 AM EST | UPDATED: November 17, 2026 at 3:50 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... After heavy overnight downpours drenched parts of Broward County, triggering a 1-in-100-year event, more bouts of storms are in store for South Florida for the next several days.
 Most of Broward County received between 8 and 15 inches of rain since Tuesday afternoon, though most of it fell between midnight and midday Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service Miami’s latest briefing. Hollywood was particularly hard-hit, with 24-hour totals between Tuesday and Wednesday at 10:30 a.m. reaching between 16 and 17.2 inches in some western areas of the city.
 “This is about a once-in-a-hundred-year type of event,” according to Will Redman, a weather service meteorologist in Miami.
 The “100-year” term describes the likelihood: There is a 1% chance of that happening in any given year.

 In addition to Hollywood, areas of Plantation and Lauderhill also recorded 24-hour rainfall totals greater than 10 inches. Cities farther west, including Cooper City, Davie, Tamarac, Weston, Lauderdale Lakes and Coconut Creek, recorded between 4 and 5.3 inches.
 Widespread additional rain of 2 to 4 inches is expected to fall from Wednesday through Saturday morning. But localized amounts “could easily reach double these estimates,” the NWS Miami warned. Some areas could again see much higher amounts of 8 to 10 inches or more, and forecasters are unclear where exactly the heaviest rains will fall.
 “Since the ground is saturated, any additional rainfall can worsen the flooding,” Redman said.
 South Florida remains under a flood watch through Thursday evening. By Saturday morning, there is a 1-in-10 chance that isolated rainfall totals reach up to 10 inches along the east coast, the “reasonable worst case” scenario in the forecast, the weather service said.
 Across South Florida, Broward was the hardest hit Tuesday.  The highest 24-hour rainfall total in Palm Beach County, at 3.4 inches at the Holey Land Wildlife Management Area, pales in comparison to Broward’s. Across Miami-Dade County, 2 to 5.3 inches were recorded by early Wednesday morning, according to the weather service’s briefing.
 A wind advisory also went into effect Wednesday afternoon after multiple areas in Broward and Palm Beach counties saw frequent gusts of wind up to 45 mph. The strongest winds reported in South Florida so far Wednesday were in Sunrise, at 58 mph.
 Lasting through early Thursday morning, the gusty winds are likely to topple unsecured objects and could cause power outages if tree limbs are blown down, according to the advisory.
 The weather service also said there are dangerous conditions along the beaches, with the potential for 30 mph wind gusts and “a high risk of life-threatening rip currents.” When it isn’t raining, expect plenty of cloud cover this week, with temperatures in the upper 70s to low 80s.
 Earlier this month, the weather service warned that a very strong El Niño during the dry season will likely bring a wetter, stormier winter than normal to South Florida. The downpours this week are the latest: Two weeks ago, downpours hammered the region, causing flooding in many communities.

 The South Florida Water Management District issued flood-related safety tips, including:
 — If you face life-threatening flooding or are in imminent danger, call 911.
— Ensure debris, trash cans and other items are secured and can’t blow into drainage ways.
— Floodwaters can hide hidden dangers: Do not wade or swim in floodwaters.
 Here’s the five-day forecast for Broward and Palm Beach counties, summarized by AI based on information from the National Weather Service. All text is reviewed and edited by our journalists. 
 Thursday: Forecasts call for showers and thunderstorms before 1 p.m., then showers and possibly a thunderstorm, mainly after 1 p.m. in Broward, while Palm Beach can expect showers, with thunderstorms also possible after 1 p.m. Highs will be around 80 degrees. Expect east winds of about 16 mph.
 Thursday night: Overnight lows will drop to around 72 degrees. A chance of rain remains overnight.
 Friday: Forecasts call for a 40% chance of showers in Broward, while Palm Beach County can expect showers likely before 1 p.m., then a chance of showers and thunderstorms between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., then a chance of showers after 4 p.m. Highs will be around 81 degrees. Expect northeast winds of about 10 mph.
 Friday night: Overnight lows will drop to around 70 degrees. A chance of rain remains overnight.
 Saturday: Forecasts call for a 20% chance of showers and thunderstorms after 1 p.m. in Broward, while Palm Beach County can expect a 30% chance of showers and thunderstorms after 1 p.m. Highs will be around 82 degrees. Expect west winds of about 7 mph.
 Saturday night: Overnight lows will drop to around 68 degrees.
 Sunday: Expect mostly sunny skies across the region. Highs will be around 81 degrees. Expect west winds of about 5 mph.
 Sunday night: Overnight lows will drop to around 67 degrees. Cloud cover continues overnight.
 Monday: Expect a 20% chance of showers across the region. Highs will be around 80 degrees.
 Monday night: Overnight lows will drop to around 69 degrees.
